about: How the grader builds, starts and talks to your twin. Fixed: never edit. Placeholders in {} are filled by the grader. Language, libraries and architecture are your choice; record it in sim/DECISION.md.

build.note: executable, run once from the repo root on a clean Linux x86_64 box (spec in the score); may fetch dependencies; must leave sim/run ready

decision_record.note: why this language, libraries and architecture; evidence means something you measured or tried

clock: every t is the twin process's monotonic clock in seconds, the same across car, tracker and admin
timing: thresholds the latency, tracker, realtime and camera checks use: car/timing.json twin

car.api: the real car's routes and responses: car/spec.json web_api
car.tls: HTTPS with a self-signed certificate, like the car; clients do not verify it

GET /pose.t: s, twin clock: the time this pose was true; served late by the tracker stage and refreshed at the tracker rate

admin.GET /admin/ready: 200 when every server and the physics loop are running
admin.GET /admin/log?since=<seq>: JSON lines of events with seq > since, oldest first; every line is {"event": <name below>, ...its fields}

request.t_recv: s: when the twin's socket had the whole request, before the simulated Wi-Fi leg
request.t_done: s: when the response left the twin's socket

applied.t: s: when the command reached the simulated servo (after onboard, ROS and PWM-frame delays)
applied.request_seq: seq of the request event that caused it

GET /admin/ticks.intervals_ms: the last >= 1000 physics tick intervals, oldest first

status: draft: fields marked in DECISIONS.md may change before version 1
